title: Schema (data-model design artifact)
description: Stage 5 (#54's flagship). ⚠️ NAME HAZARD, stated once and loudly: this is the PROJECT'S data-model design artifact — the thing rendered as an ER diagram. It is NOT the meta-format governing planning artifacts, which is JSON Schema 2020-12 (#82). The file name `schema.schema.json` is the collision made visible: the outer `.schema.json` is the meta-format, the inner `schema` is #38's artifact type. See #86 — if the blur bites in practice, the type renames to `data-model` and the prefix stays SCH.

payload.description: The definition file. #8: 'a schema is a definition file, rendered as an ER diagram — not a diagram that happens to look like a schema.' The format is DECLARED, not invented: this artifact deliberately does not model tables, columns, types, keys or relations, because doing so would be a second schema language written for no reason other than that the artifact is called `schema`.

format.description: Adding a format is a decision, not a convenience: each one needs a parser for the ER rendering and for the handoff. A format nothing renders is a payload nobody sees.

summary.description: What this data model covers, in a line or two. Human orientation only.

storageTarget.description: Where this model is intended to live — stage 5's exit criterion is 'data model approved; storage target chosen', so the choice belongs on the artifact rather than in prose. #45 applies where a model is storage-agnostic.

decidedBy.description: Decisions that shaped this model — normalisation, storage target, identity strategy.

derivedFrom.description: A model this one extends or specialises. Same-type edge, so it always resolves.

x-wrapsExternalFormat.description: Entities, fields, types, keys, indexes and relations live in the definition file at payload.path and are validated by that format's own tooling. If a field is proposed here that the payload format already expresses, it is the duplication this annotation refuses. `storageTarget` is the one exception and is deliberate: it is a PLANNING fact about the model rather than a fact expressible inside it, and stage 5's exit criterion checks it.
x-wrapsExternalFormat.validatedBy: the payload format's own validator, invoked by the lint (#47)

x-unresolvableTraceTargets.description: #75 in force: evidence, assertion and question are not among step 3's activated four.
